title: Azimuth runway & HC tuning playbook (prototype)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working prototype — not final — for a small, actionable playbook to (a) buy additional runway efficiently by tuning headcount phasing and (b) define rapid pricing sensitivity levers we can flip as token demand or GPU costs deviate from base assumptions. Focus is Q2–Q4 2026 operational horizon.

Key constraints we assume (base case):
- Net burn target: $3.6M / quarter (org-level cash cadence)
- Token demand growth: +20% q/q baseline, with 3 scenarios (down -10%, base +20%, up +50%)
- GPU unit cost (weighted across regions): $1.02 / GPU-hour effective after discounts
- Headcount hiring lag: hire-to-onboard = 8 weeks; ramp productivity = 12 weeks
- Committed capacity (reserved) vs on-demand mix: 60/40 in base

What the playbook does:
1) Fast HC phasing knobs (nonlinear): shift 6 roles to delayed start dates (2–3 month push) to capture $1.2M gross cash savings in 90 days if needed. Prioritize hires with longest open-to-impact timelines (infra ops, tooling) and keep product/customer-facing ICs on schedule.
2) Pricing sensitivity triggers: small, staged price increases by customer cohort and per-route SLO (nonlinear tolerance). We enumerate routes where a modest price lift (3–7%) materially improves per-token margin without expected churn: embeddings batch, high-temp exploratory generation, and experimental repack routes.
3) Capacity mix swaps: move 10% of burst traffic to spot GPUs in non-critical regions and enable model quantization profiles for low-SLA workloads to reduce per-token compute by 12–18%.

Scenario matrix (short description):
- Scenario A: Demand down -10% q/q (stress). Actions: immediate freeze on noncritical hiring, accelerate price experiments for premium routes, convert 15% reserved -> cancel increments where contract allows; deploy immediate quantization pilot on 2 model clusters. Expected runway extension: +4–6 months.
- Scenario B: Base (plan). Actions: follow planned hiring; run controlled price A/B on 2 routes; maintain reserved mix. Runway: baseline.
- Scenario C: Demand spike +50%. Actions: accelerate burst pool capacity, tighten per-customer quotas for free credits, open a one-off higher-commit product for large consumers. Expected incremental revenue: covers 60% of extra GPU spend if converted to commit.

Tactical headcount plan (calls and micro-decisions):
- Categorize all open reqs into 3 buckets: critical-customer (no delay), latency-savings (can defer 6–12w), productivity/tooling (defer 12–24w).
- Quick wins: pause 8 contractor conversions in productivity bucket (saves ~ $420k Q).
- Contingent hires: convert 3 SRE roles to 6-month contractors with higher day-rate but no full-time benefits, net cash smoothing of ~$200k near-term.

Pricing sensitivity playbook (how we experiment quickly):
- Micro-A/B framework: pick 1 region + 2 low-risk routes, run 3% price lift for 7 days, monitor usage and net new signups. If revenue change > 5% with <1.2% churn -> roll to 5% for 14 days.
- Cohort-based uplift: enterprise accounts with SLA contracts exempt unless negotiated; self-serve customers get first-experiment exposure. Place soft caps on free credit assignments to avoid noise.
- Communications: prewrite short-FAQ and support playbook so CS can proactively message impacted customers for predictable churn management.

Compute / model-tech levers (cost side):
- Quantization profiles: we have 3 candidate quantized variants for large models (Q2 pilot shows 12% lower token compute with ~1% quality delta on eval sets). Rollout plan: enable for background embeddings and non-SLA chat routes.
- Batch vs latency policy: increase max batch horizon from 30ms -> 65ms for non-interactive routes to gain 8–10% throughput improvement. Toggle via per-route config; measure latency-sensitive route impact in canary.
- Kernel & region routing: prefer cheaper region pools for template/embeds workload (auto-route); this is a soft knob we can flip in hours. Expected short-term savings: ~7%.

Simple financial impact sketch (text table):
- Baseline quarterly burn: $3.6M
- Deferred HC (6 roles): saves $1.2M in cash payroll runrate (phased)
- Quantization + spot mix: estimated savings $420k / quarter if scaled to 30% of traffic
- Pricing lift pilot: if successful, +$250–600k incremental revenue (varies by uptake)
Net effect if all executed in stress: save/earn ~ $2.0M in quarter -> runway extension roughly +5 months.

Decision gate framework (quick):
- Gate 0 (signal): 2 consecutive weeks of realized token consumption < 90% of forecast OR 7-day GPU spot price index +15% -> convene finance + exec prep.
- Gate 1 (action): hold noncritical hiring and trigger 3% price AB test -> 72-hour review window on telemetry.
- Gate 2 (escalation): if burn still > target after two review cycles, defer further hiring, and increase spot mix to 20% for non-critical clusters.

Open questions / risks (working):
- Churn sensitivity: self-serve cohort elasticity unknown for 3–7% price lift; we only have coarse historical signals. Need a small controlled sample before org-wide rollout.
- Contractual constraints: some reserved cancellations have penalties > 30d notice — need legal check on each SKU.
- Product impact: deferring productivity hires slows some Optimize roadmap items (model-suggested quant profiles) and may blunt medium-term cost improvements.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Finance: produce token-customer elasticity quick cohort model (Miguel). Due 2026-03-20.
- Eng infra: list reserved commitments with cancellation windows and penalty matrix (Rina + infra). Due 2026-03-22.
- SRE/Product: identify 2 safe candidate routes for 3% AB test and prepare canary config (Samira). Due 2026-03-24.
- Legal: quick review of reserved contract termination clauses flagged by infra list. Due 2026-03-26.

Notes to self / context:
- This is intentionally tactical and conservative — objective is cash runway rather than feature completeness. Keep messaging simple to Exec: two levers (HC phasing, small targeted price tests) + compute optimization pilots.
- Keep one person accountable per action item and keep weekly 15m sync until Gate 1 cleared.

Appendix: quick checklist for an AB price experiment (ops checklist):
- Choose cohort (region + route) and generate control/variant billing keys
- Create 3% price variant via billing config; set TTL 7d with auto-rollback flag if churn spike>2%
- Notify CS and support with canned replies
- Instrument: token volume, active accounts, MRR delta, churn events, NPS/feedback tag capture
- Postmortem: 3 business-day writeup + decision (rollback, expand, escalate)

End of doc. This is a short-lived working paper — copy to Confluence once validated and label as PROTOTYPE.
